back: A thread-like structure of DNA, found in the nucleus, that carries genes.
A nucleus with two sets of chromosomes; in humans 46, in 23 pairs.
A nucleus with a single set of unpaired chromosomes; in human gametes, 23.
Nuclear division giving rise to genetically identical cells.
notes: The chromosome number stays the same.

back: Growth, repair of tissues, replacement of worn-out cells and asexual reproduction.

front: What happens to chromosomes before and during mitosis?
back: Before: each chromosome is copied exactly. During: the copies separate, one to each new nucleus.
An unspecialised cell that divides by mitosis to produce cells that can become specialised.
notes: Example: bone marrow cells that make blood cells.

back: A reduction division that halves the chromosome number from diploid to haploid, producing genetically different cells.
Gametes must be haploid so fertilisation restores the diploid number (23 + 23 = 46); it also produces variation.
Humans: testes and ovaries. Flowering plants: anthers and ovules.
Mitosis: 2 identical cells, same chromosome number. Meiosis: 4 different cells, half the chromosome number.
